snapshot.restore: restoreShift validates a saved snapshot; invalid data is removed and replaced with createInitialShift.
snapshot.save: serializeShift writes each reducer state change after restoration completes.
snapshot.reset: Remove the versioned snapshot and restore initial shift, first forecast, steady posture, and closed mobile drawer.

sequence: settle shift and open House Book

recovery.renderFrom: RecoveryOffer.actions in order; match RecoveryOffer.costs by action for ticks, freshness, and ledger cost.
recovery.invariant: No universal fixed action pair; an open offer must resolve before deterministic progress continues.

settlement.invariant: Settled state is immutable; margin is restaurant health, not a transferable reward.

components.name: Signal Stage
components.description: One fixed marquee stage with lamp, icon, and label; lit state never relies on hue alone.
components.css: .ds-signal-stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:49px auto;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;min-height:72px;border:2px solid #5c491c;border-radius:4px;background:#caa62f url('/materials/marquee-enamel.webp') center/cover;color:var(--ink,#16191d);font:700 1.35rem 'Big Shoulders Variable','Arial Narrow',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.035em}.ds-signal-lamp{display:grid;width:49px;height:49px;place-items:center;border-radius:50%;background:#2b2c24 url('/materials/indicator-lamp.webp') center/150%;filter:grayscale(.76) brightness(.43);box-shadow:0 3px 5px rgb(0 0 0 / 50%);font:800 .8rem 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable',sans-serif}.ds-is-lit .ds-signal-lamp{background-color:#f0a31f;background-blend-mode:screen;filter:sepia(.35) saturate(1.42) brightness(1.32);box-shadow:inset 0 0 14px rgb(255 244 188 / 42%),0 0 19px rgb(255 183 57 / 55%)}.ds-signal-stage:focus-within{outline:3px solid var(--focus,#91d8ff);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Forecast Ticket

components.name: Physical Route Gate

components.name: Reducer Recovery Action

narrative.overview:
Fry Signal is a cheerful 1960s drive-through control room rebuilt as a late-night electromechanical routing instrument. The interface is one bolted machine: dark steel casing, fryer-paper tickets, enamel plates, lamps, switches, rails, and compact operator labels all belong to the same physical object. It must feel handled and dependable, not nostalgic for its own sake.

The route is the game. A forecast sits at the left edge, the continuous side-on track network owns the center, and an exception rail occupies the right. BATCH / PACK / GO is the fixed marquee grammar above that instrument. Operational state is communicated with position, route geometry, shape, label, lamp count, and motion together; color adds character but never carries meaning alone.

The raster materials are authored finish layers, while all words, controls, icons, paths, bags, vehicles, and order marks remain semantic HTML, CSS, or SVG. The six shipped materials have fixed roles: riveted steel frames the shell, dark panels, and shift-progress row; aged ticket paper skins forecasts, bags, the exception rail, commit drawer, reset control, service summaries, and House Book; marquee enamel gives painted signs, state plates, recovery actions, and deterministic progress their worn coating; indicator lamp supplies lamp glass and hardware; dimensional track forms the rail fill; and route switch makes gates read as physical levers.
keyCharacteristics: One monolithic instrument rather than a collection of floating dashboard cards.
Worn steel, aged paper, painted enamel, inset rails, visible fasteners, and restrained grime.
A dominant route topology with forecast and exception context held at its edges.
Condensed roadside display type paired with highly legible operator text.
Shape-plus-label signals, crisp vehicle silhouettes, fixed marquee stages, and explicit costs.
Tactile state changes with bounded motion and complete reduced-motion equivalents.
Deterministic local progress, versioned save truth, and a settlement-only House Book.

rules.name: The Scarce Lamp Rule
rules.body: Marquee yellow marks the current decision or active stage; it is not a generic decoration or background wash.

rules.name: The Redundant Signal Rule
rules.body: Every status color must travel with a stable label, shape, position, pattern, or route change.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders names the machine and its stations; Atkinson explains what is happening and what an action costs.

rules.name: The Operator Copy Rule
rules.body: Small text may be compact, but never vague: action, consequence, duration, and status remain explicit.

rules.name: The Continuous Board Rule
rules.body: Responsive adaptation may compress context into drawers or sheets, but it never replaces the route board with hidden task pages.

rules.name: The No-Drag Rule
rules.body: Every essential route choice is a button reachable by keyboard, touch, or pointer; route operation never depends on dragging.

rules.name: The Mounted-Plate Rule
rules.body: Elevation expresses how a piece is fastened to the instrument; nothing floats without a mechanical reason.

rules.name: The Hardware Radius Rule
rules.body: Keep corners tight enough to read as enamel plate, ticket, or chassis; large soft card radii break the instrument illusion.

rules.name: The Reducer Terms Rule
rules.body: Recovery names, availability, and costs come from the current RecoveryOffer; never hard-code a universal pair or stale consequence copy in the interface.

rules.name: The Local Truth Rule
rules.body: State text distinguishes “Restoring local shift…” from “Saved locally” and displays both fixture and rules versions; local persistence is never described as account, server, or chain authority.

rules.name: The Settlement Receipt Rule
rules.body: The House Book reports one immutable reducer result after the final recovery window; it never forecasts, animates, or implies external ownership.

dos: Do make every new surface look mounted into the same Mile 42 instrument through steel framing, paper or enamel plates, hard borders, and purposeful depth.
Do keep the route topology primary and express decisions through named gates, visible paths, destinations, and explicit costs.
Do pair color with shape, pattern, position, count, icon, and accessible text.
Do use Big Shoulders for station-like display roles and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for operational meaning.
Do preserve the responsive forecast drawer, continuous route board, anchored exception sheet, safe-area clearance, reduced motion, and forced-colors behavior.
Do render progress, recovery terms, service condition, and House Book values from the reducer state that owns them.
Do keep local restore, saved, reset, final-recovery, and settled states explicit in control copy.
donts: Don't break the interface into generic floating dashboard cards, soft pills, glass panels, or interchangeable SaaS controls.
Don't turn ordinary batching, packing, or dispatch into repeated minigames or repeat HOLD / LOOP / SEND controls on every bag.
Don't present recovery as a score bonus, hide its cost, or use money-first status in the live service HUD.
Don't assume every recovery is Loopback Save plus Pull Forward; render the current offer's action and cost arrays.
Don't show the House Book before settlement or imply that its margin is transferable, remote, or chain-authoritative.
Don't represent crew as capacity counters, collectible upgrades, or disposable production units.
Don't use a mascot panel in the live HUD or let raster assets carry required text or state.
Don't hide the route board on mobile or require drag, animation, or color perception to operate it.
